what_it_does: 5G and 6G base stations need to efficiently deliver power to radio antennas across many transmitters (massive MIMO arrays). This chip uses a gallium-nitride (GaN) semiconductor to implement digital envelope tracking—a technique that separates power delivery into two stages. The first stage slowly generates multiple voltage levels efficiently using switched power converters. The second stage quickly adjusts the output voltage to match what the radio transmitter needs, moment by moment. Using multiple voltage levels instead of just switching between two extremes reduces electrical noise ripple and losses. The design runs on 48 volts and can deliver 74 watts, which is the scale needed for base-station power amplifiers, and GaN integration on a single die keeps power loss and heat manageable.
